AVALON CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  TUESDAY, APRIL 1, 2025— 5:00 PM
  410 AVALON CANYON ROAD
  AGENDA
In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting,
please contact the City Clerk’s Office (310) 510-022. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City
to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All
public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the public inspection at the time the records
are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members of the City Council. Such records shall be available at City Hall
located at 410 Avalon Canyon Rd.

 For the public’s convenience, but not participation, the meeting can be viewed:
  On local cable: Catalina Broadband Solutions channel 3
  Streaming on Facebook Live: www.facebook.com/CityOfAvalonOfficial
  Streaming on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/CityofAvalonCA

CALL TO ORDER I PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE I INVOCATION I ROLL CALL

PRESENTATION
  1. A Proclamation will be presented to the Varsity Head Coach Nick Morones and the Avalon
  High School Football Team recognizing their accomplishment as 2024 CIF Southern
  Section 8-Man Division II Champions.

ANNOUNCEMENTS I WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

DEPARTMENT HEAD REPORTS

CITY MANAGER REPORT I CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

COUNCILMEMBER REPORTSIREQUESTS I MAYOR REPORT

ORAL COMMUNICATION
Members of the public may address the City Council at this time. No action will be taken on non-
agenda items at this meeting. Speakers should limit comments to two (2) minutes each.

CONSENT CALENDAR

1.  Warrants
  Expenditures Submitted for Approval:
  • US Bank General Account Warrants totaling $1,037,903.52.
  • One payroll totaling $261,855.24.
  • Four electronic fund transfers totaling $53,661 .26.
  Recommended Action
  Approve total expenditures for March 10, 2025 through March 21, 2025 totaling
  $1,353,420.02.

2.  Declare old vehicles and equipment as surplus
  Historically, the City Council is presented with a list of items that are surplus, the Council
  declares it surplus, and then the declared items are either sold via Public Surplus, given
  to charity, or disposed of properly.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution declaring vehicles & equipment listed in resolution as surplus property
  and authorize the City Manager to dispose of it in accordance with City policy.

3.  2024 General Plan Housing Element Annual Progress Report
  Government Code §65400 mandates each elected board submit an annual progress
  report to the California Department of Housing and Community Development and the
  Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation on the status and progress of the
  City’s Housing Element implementation.
  Recommended Action
  Receive and file the General Plan Housing Element Annual Report for 2024 and direct
  staff to submit the Housing Element Annual Progress Report to the California Department
  of Housing and Community Development and the Governor’s Office of Lane Use and
  Climate Innovation.

GENERAL BUSINESS

4.  On-Site Professionalized Services for a 5-Year Fire Hydrant Flow Test and Inspection
  The City maintains freshwater and saltwater fire hydrants serving as critical components
  of the fire protection system. Fire hydrants should be inspected and flow tested every five
  years ensuring operational readiness and adequate fire flow capacity.
  Recommended Action
  Per the City’s procurement policy, authorize the City Manager or designee, to execute an
  agreement with Davis Fire Protection to provide on-site professionalized services for a 5-
  Year Fire Hydrant Flow Test and Inspection of approximately 200 fire hydrants in the City
  of Avalon for an amount not-to-exceed $25,000 from the Saltwater Capital Improvement
  Fund 11325-6552.

5.  Type Ill Engine Purchase
  On March 18, 2025 the City Council authorized the City to enter into an agreement with
  Edison International for reimbursement of a wildland fire engine for a not to exceed sum
  of $600,000. City Staff have researched appropriate vehicles that could supplement the
  current Fire Department fleet by providing an option more suitable for wildland fire
  emergencies with four-wheel drive capabilities.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to negotiate and execute a contract with
  South Coast Fire Equipment for a not-to-exceed sum of $700,000 as budgeted in the
  City’s Fiscal Year 2024-25, Capital Improvement Project # 234501, Account #1 0245-
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
APRIL 1, 2025
PAGE 3

  6871. 2. Amend the Capital Improvement Project # 234501, Account #10245-6871 by
  increasing the budget by $600,000 to offset the anticipated donation from Edison
  International.

6.  Authorize the Purchase of an Off Road Emergency Response Vehicle
  Noting an increase in need for off road calls for service, City Staff have researched small,
  mobile vehicles with off-road capabilities. In the past the Fire Department has used a
  Ford Utility Pick-up truck for calls on the hour trail, or other off road locations; however,
  this vehicle is not suited for emergency calls for service. Additionally, none of the City’s
  ambulances can maneuver the hour trail or other off road locations safely.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to purchase a 2025 Honda Pioneer 1000
  and MEDLITE Transport Deluxe (MTD-103) Rescue Bed for an amount not to exceed
  $35,000 from Capital Improvement Project #234501, Account #10245-6871 from
  Huntington Beach Honda.

7.  Medical Cannabis Delivery Business Permit Application Direction
  Per City Council direction, the City reopened the application process for Medical
  Cannabis Delivery Business Permits on January 24, 2025. The second application period
  was scheduled to run from January 24, 2025 to March 10, 2025; however, on March 3,
  2025 City Staff extended the application deadline to March 21, 2025 at 4 p.m.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the finding that the City received one complete application for the Medical
  Cannabis Delivery Services Business Permit by the stated deadline March 21, 2025 at
  —

  4 p.m. 2. Make the affirmative finding to reject an incomplete application received after
  the stated deadline.

8.  Award a Contract to Replace Piles on the Green Pleasure Pier and Club Dingy Dock
  In 2025, the City developed a plan to replace piles on the Green Pleasure Pier by marine
  barge. The plan would have significantly less impact on the commercial businesses on
  the pier, as well as provide a convenient, dedicated and secure space for a contractor to
  maintain tools and supplies associated with the job. Knowing the most substantial
  expense of the project is associated with mobilization and demobilization costs, the City
  put together a tiered bid schedule that recognizes a singular mobilization and
  demobilization and prioritizes pile replacement by package.
  Recommended Action
  Award a contract to the lowest responsible bidder to complete the scope of work identified
  by City Staff for the Green Pleasure Pier Pile Replacement Program.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
APRIL 1, 2025
PAGE 4

9.  Discuss Revisions to Article 3 of Chapter 1 of Title 3 of the Avalon Municipal Code
  Modifying the Transient Rental Licensing System
  In 2023, the City Council adopted an Urgency Ordinance #U-121223 establishing a
  moratorium on the issuance of new Transient Rental Licenses. During the moratorium
  period City Staff have worked to determine how to proceed with potential revisions the
  Transient Rental Licensing System.
  Recommended Action
  Review and discuss alternatives. If consensus, recommend the Planning Commission
  consider ordinance revisions regarding transient rental license regulations, and direct
  staff to revise the ordinance.

ADJOURN

NOTICE OF POSTING

I, Devin Elise Hart, declare that the City Council Agenda for Tuesday, April 1, 2025 was posted
on Friday, March 28, 2025 on the City’s website, www.cityofavalon.com/agendacenter, and at
City Hall, 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

Devin Elise Hart, Senior Management Analyst

SUBJECT:  2024 General Plan Housing Element Annual Progress Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Receive and file the General Plan Housing Element
Annual Report for 2024 and direct staff to submit the Housing Element Annual Progress
Report to the Cahfornia Department of Housing and Community Development and the
Governor’s Office of Lane Use and Climate Innovation.

REPORT SUMMARY: Government Code §65400 mandates each elected board submit
an annual progress report (APR) to the California Department of Housing and Community
Development (HCD) and the Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation ([CI)
on the status and progress of the City’s Housing Element implementation. The report
assists HCD with tracking a jurisdiction’s progress toward meeting its regional housing
needs assessment (RHNA) allocation. It also provides LCI information to assist with
identifying statewide trends in land use decision-making and how local planning activities
relate to statewide planning goals and policies. APRs may also identify necessary
modifications and improvements to General Plan guidelines.

Submitting the City’s annual housing progress report to HCD and LCI fulfills statutory
requirements to report housing planning and development progress in meeting local
housing needs. Prior to submittal to the State, the annual report must be presented to the
City Council for review and acceptance.

One planning application for the Cameron Hotel at 301 Beacon Street (PC#2842) was
approved by City Council on November 5, 2024, which includes construction of three new
employee housing units (two new two-bedroom apartments and one studio manager unit
for employee housing). One apartment and the studio manager unit are required to be
constructed during Phase 1 of project construction, which has an SCE water allocation.

No building permits were issued for new residential units in 2024. Two new residential
units were issued a final inspection in 2024:

  •  211 Mar de Cortez (one 6-bedroom single-family residence)
  •  240 Catalina Avenue (two apartments and one ADU)

More detailed information about unit affordability assumptions and the City’s progress in
meeting its Year 202 1-2029 RHNA goals is provided in Attachment 1.
 FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Affordable Housing

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City would
be out of compliance with State guidelines.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Submit the City’s Housing annual progress reports to the HCD
and LCI.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

MEETING DATE:  April 1 2025  AGENDA ITEM:

ORIGINATING DEP:  Public Works  CITY MANAGER:  LtLA
PREPARED BY:  Jackeline Cordero, Public Works Director

SUBJECT:  On-Site Professionalized Services for a 5-Year Fire Hydrant Flow
  Test and Inspection.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Per the City’s procurement policy, authorize the City Manager
or designee, to execute an agreement with Davis Fire Protection to provide on-site
professionalized services for a 5-Year Fire Hydrant Flow Test and Inspection of approximately
200 fire hydrants in the City of Avalon for an amount not-to-exceed $25,000 from the Saltwater
Capital Improvement Fund 11325-6552.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon maintains a network of freshwater and saltwater fire
hydrants serving as critical components of the fire protection system. Per NFPA (National Fire
Protection Association) 291 guidelines and industry best practices, fire hydrants should be
inspected and flow tested every five years ensuring operational readiness and adequate fire flow
capacity. The saltwater hydrants require additional maintenance due to the corrosive water going
through the system, making the inspection of the hydrants essential for system reliability.

Services for this project are included in the FY 24-25 Budget  —  Saltwater Capital Improvement
Fund 11325-6552 for an amount of not-to-exceed $25,000.

Staff requested and received three proposals from Davis Fire Protection, PERC Water, and
Utility Systems Science and Software. The three companies were asked to provide proposals
for fresh and saltwater fire hydrant flow testing and inspection services. Davis Fire Protection
was the lowest, responsible bidder with costs totaling $25,000.

Obtaining three proposals fulfilled the informal bid competitive process specified in the Avalon
Municipal Code (AMC) Section 3-4.106(a).

  Company  Location  Proposed Cost
  Fire Davis Protection  Huntington Beach, CA  $25,000
  PERC Water  Fountain Valley, CA  $52,192
  Utility Systems Science &  Santa Ana, CA  $75,573
  Software

To meet regulatory and operational requirements, the City seeks approval to enter into a contract
with Davis Fire Protection to perform the following scope of work:
  1. Flow Fire Hydrants and Gather GPM Readings.
   2.  Deliver NFPA Chapter 7 Title 19 Report.
  3.  Dichlorination of Water Being Flowed.
  4.  Exercise All Valves on Property Feeding Fire Hydrants.
  5.  Any additional hydrants will be billed at $125.00 each.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Total expenditure is not-to-exceed $25,000. Funds are allocated in FY 24-
25 Saltwater Capital Improvement Fund 11325-6552.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Improved readiness and reliability of the City’s fire protection system, fire
hydrants.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Fire suppression
efforts would be delayed during emergency fire events and the City would not be complaint with
NFPA standards. Performing routine fire hydrant inspections and flow testing is a critical public
safety measure.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Authorize the City Manager or designee, to execute an agreement with
Davis Fire Protection to provide on-site professionalized services for a 5-Year Fire Hydrant Flow
Test and Inspection of approximately 200 fire hydrants in the City of Avalon as requested.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

The fire hydrant pressure and flow test is a critical procedure conducted to assess
the water supply available for firefighting operations. This test helps determine the
static pressure, residual pressure, and flow rate of water from a fire hydrant, which
are essential for fire protection systems and ensuring adequate water supply during
emergencies.

Key Components of the Test

1. Static Pressure: This is the pressure in the water system when no water is
flowing. ft is measured by closing all nearby hydrants and valves to ensure no water
is being drawn from the system.

2. Residual Pressure: This is the pressure remaining in the system while water is
flowing from one or more hydrants. It is measured at the same time as the flow
rate.

3. Flow Rate: This is the volume of water that can be delivered from the hydrant,
typically measured in gallons per minute (GPM) or liters per minute (LPM).

Steps to Conduct a Fire Hydrant Pressure and Flow Test

1. Preparation:
  - Notify the local water authority and any affected parties.
  - Ensure all necessary equipment is available, including pressure gauges, pitot
tubes, and flow meters.
  - Identify the hydrants to be tested, including the test hydrant and nearby
hydrants. (To be determined by Avalon).

2. Measuring Static Pressure:
  -Close all nearby hydrants and valves to ensure no water is flowing.
  -Attach a pressure gauge to the test hydrant.
  -Record the static pressure reading.

3. Measuring Flow Rate and Residual Pressure:
  -Open the test hydrant fully and allow water to flow.
  -Use a pitot tube to measure the velocity of the water stream, which can be
converted to flow rate.
  -Attach a pressure gauge to a nearby hydrant to measure the residual pressure
while the test hydrant is flowing.
  -Record both the flow rate and residual pressure.

4. Calculating Results:
  -Use the collected data to calculate the available water supply. This often
involves using hydraulic formulas or software to determine the systems capacity.
  -Compare the results with local fire code requirements and the needs of the fire
protection system.

SUBJECT:  Authorize the Purchase of an Off Road Emergency Response
  Vehicle

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to purchase a
2025 Honda Pioneer 1000 and MEDLITE Transport Deluxe (MTD-103) Rescue Bed for an
amount not to exceed $35,000 from Capital Improvement Project #234501, Account #1 0245-
6871 from Huntington Beach Honda.

REPORT SUMMARY: Noting an increase in need for off road calls for service, City Staff have
researched small, mobile vehicles with off-road capabilities. In the past the Fire Department has
used a Ford Utility Pick-up truck for calls on the hour trail, or other off road locations; however,
this vehicle is not suited for emergency calls for service. Additionally, none of the City’s
ambulances can maneuver the hour trail or other off road locations safely.

Working with the Catalina Island Search and Rescue Team, as well as through discussions with
other fire departments throughout Southern California, City Staff has identified the Honda
Pioneer 1000, 6 seat, off road utility vehicle as the most suitable option. The back two seats of
this vehicle can be removed and a MEDLITE Transport Deluxe (MTD-103) Rescue Bed can be
added to safely handle a patient and one more passengers as well as four emergency first
responders.

In addition to its off road capabilities and use, the vehicle can be utilized when town is congested
and a full size apparatus cannot maneuver busy streets (ie. during the 4th of July parade, or other
events). Also, there are other areas of town that are difficult to drive a full size apparatus, such
as the Terraces and areas of the Memorial/Divide Road.

Per the City of Avalon’s procurement policy, Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.106 (a), the City
requested quotes from qualified vendors:

City Staff recommend the City Council authorizes the City Manager, or his designee, to purchase
a 2025 Honda Pioneer 1000 and MEDLITE Transport Deluxe (MTD-103) Rescue Bed for an
amount not to exceed $35,000 from Huntington Beach Honda as the lowest responsive bidder.
Huntington Beach Honda has the vehicle in stock, ready to ship, and is the only vendor that can
also provide the MEDLITE bed. The total cost of the vehicle and MEDLITE bed from Huntington
Beach Honda will be less than if the equipment was procured separately.

The Catalina Island Search and Rescue Team has committed to donating $13,000 for the
procurement of this vehicle. The remaining balance will be remitted from Capital Improvement
Project # 234501, Account #10245-6871.

SUBJECT:  Medical Cannabis Delivery Business Permit Application Direction

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Make the finding that the City received one complete
application for the Medical Cannabis Delivery Services Business Permit by the stated deadline
— March 21, 2025 at 4 p.m. 2. Make the affirmative finding to reject an incomplete application
received after the stated deadline.

REPORT SUMMARY: On January 21, 2025, the City Council authorized Staff to open the
application process for a potential new medical cannabis delivery business permit holder. This
was the second application period since October 22, 2024. During the first application period  —

October 22, 2024 to December 16, 2024  the City received two incomplete applications
  —

before the deadline. On the date of the deadline, two entities provided incomplete applications
with one of the two entities providing the remaining portion of the application by the following
day. Both entities paid the required application fee before the deadline. Despite one entity
curing the incomplete application, on January 21, 2025, the City Council made the affirmative
finding that no applications were received by the deadline and rejected all proposals.

Per City Council direction, the City reopened the application process on January 24, 2025. The
second application period was scheduled to run from January 24, 2025 to March 10, 2025;
however, on March 3, 2025 City Staff extended the application deadline to March 21, 2025 at 4
p.m.

The City received all components of an application, including application fee and live scan
results, from Catalina Cannabis LLC on March 13, 2025.

Around 3:50 p.m. on March 21, 2025, the City was contacted by a representative from Catalina
Cannabis Company regarding the application deadline and submission process. A partial
application was delivered to City Hall at 4:08 p.m.(technically after the deadline). At that time,
the application fee was paid. At 5:04 p.m. additional components of the application were
delivered via email. At the time this report was authored, elements of the application  —

including an interior floor plan of the proposed premises, photographs accurately depicting the
entire interior and exterior of the site, etc. remain outstanding. It should be noted, City Staff
  —

have made no attempt to contact either applicant regarding their application or its level of
completeness.
 Before City Staff begin a more comprehensive analysis of the applications submitted, City Staff
need to determine which applications may be considered. Per the City Attorney’s Office, since
the previous late applications have been rejected, the late application submitted by Catalina
Cannabis Company must be rejected.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: City Staff will not
have clear direction on how to process the applications received.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: City Staff will begin review of the application(s) by the process outlined
in Resolution No. 18-07 and bring the findings of the evaluation to the City Council at the April
15, 2025 City Council Meeting.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: Pursuant to the Brown Act.

  Club Dingy Dock

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Award a contract to the lowest responsible bidder to complete
the scope of work identified by City Staff for the Green Pleasure Pier Pile Program (RFP-180049-
B).

REPORT SUMMARY: Since 2018, City Staff has been working on a long term maintenance
plan for the Green Pleasure Pier. Currently maintenance work on the pier is accomplished by
City forces where feasible, but there is a limit to the size and scope of a project. When the size
and scope becomes too large, a contractor is necessary.

In 2022, the City Council awarded a contract for the Green Pleasure Pier 2022 Repair Project to
Jilk Heavy Construction, Inc. for a not to exceed amount of $266,980.00. This project replaced
five pier pilings. The repairs required portions of the pier to be closed intermittently to pedestrian
traffic; however, the City worked with the contractor to ensure that the businesses on the pier
remained open throughout the project.

In 2025, the City developed a plan to replace piles on the Green Pleasure Pier by marine barge.
The plan would have significantly less impact on the commercial businesses on the pier, as well
as provide a convenient, dedicated and secure space for a contractor to maintain tools and
supplies associated with the job. Understanding there is a significant amount of work to be
completed on the pier, the FY 2024-25 Capital Improvement Plan allocates $1,000,000 between
two projects Project #1 80049 allocates $450,000 for pile replacement and Project #247004
  —

allocates $600,000 for replacement of the deck surface of the pier.

At this time, 21 pier piles 5 fender piles and 16 structural piles need to be replaced; however,
  —  —

the level of urgency to replace these piles, varies from pile to pile. Knowing the most substantial
expense of the project is associated with mobilization and demobilization costs, the City put
together a tiered bid schedule that recognizes a singular mobilization and demobilization and
prioritizes pile replacement by package. The package order is prioritized by the need for
replacement and its location to other piles that need replacement. The REP organized pile
replacement on the pier into four packages:
  • Pier Package #1 Five (5) Piles five fender piles in the center of the pier on the outer west

  and east edges (FP-3, FP-4E, FP-1W, FP-9W) and one structural timber pile on the western
  shore side edge of the pier (9-1).

possible after loss.

work areas to prevent any unpermitted material from entering the Pacific Ocean.

The permittee shall comply with the following requirements related to the use of pressure-treated
wood in the marine environment:

  1.  New pressure-treated pile installed shall be wrapped (with fiberglass, epoxy resin
  composite, or High-density polyethylene (HDPE) wrap, etc.) extending the entire
  length of the pile and sealed completely to prevent any leaching of preservative
  chemicals into coastal waters. Any place where the protective wrap is required to be
  punctured (e.g., for mounting hardware, attaching cross bracing, or attaching bumpers
  to fender piles) shall be sealed thoroughly with epoxy suited to the marine
  environment.

  2.  Pressure-treated wood used in construction of the project shall meet the American
  Wood Protection Association’s (AWPA) wood preservative standards, specifically
  AWPA Standard Ui, the primary specification for pressure-treated wood

  3. Ammoniacal copper zinc arsenate (ACZA) pressure-treated wood shall be treated to
  the proper preservative retention standard (i.e., amount of preservative) specified by
  the AWPA for the appropriate AWPA Use Category. The ACZA pressure-treated wood
  used for the project shall not have a preservative retention exceeding the minimum
  specified for the appropriate Use Category, in order to minimize the amount of
  preservative present in treated wood on-site that may subsequently leach into the
  marine environment

  4. The ACZA pressure-treated wood shall be inspected on-site to assure it is free of
  visible surface residues or bleeding of preservatives. If ACZA pressure-treated wood

  5. The ACZA pressure-treated wood shall be stored in a contained area within a
  continuous, plastic-lined berm on the deck of the materia!s barge or the staging area.
  If there is a chance of precipitation, the wood shall be stored under a covered area or
  tarp to prevent exposure to precipitation or run-on wastes from surrounding areas. No
  runoff from the pressure treated wood storage area shall be allowed to drain to the
  marine environment.

  6. Whenever possible, cutting or drilling of ACZA pressure-treated wood shall be
  performed at a site a minimum of 100 feet away from the water, to minimize transport
  of debris and sawdust by wind to the marine environment. Any resulting sawdust, drill
  shavings, and wood scraps shall be contained and collected immediately, in order to
  prevent the discharge of pressure-treated wood to the marine environment. If it is
  essential that treated wood be cut or drilled in place on the pier, a protective layer shall
  be installed between the activity and the receiving waters so that all sawdust,
  shavings, and wood scraps generated during construction will be collected and
  prevented from entering the water below.

  7. The procedures outlined in AWPA Standard M4, Standard for the Care of
  Preservative-Treated Wood Products, shall be followed when applying a topical (non
  pressure treated) preservative to the cut ends of treated wood. Whenever possible,
  application of a topical preservative to treated wood shall be performed at a site a
  minimum of 100 feet away from the water, equipped with containment for potential
  drips and spills, in order to prevent discharge of the preservative to the environment.
  The topical preservative shall not be applied during rain events. Any excess topical
  preservative shall be wiped off, and the preservative shall be allowed to fully dry before
  the wood is used in construction. If a small amount of touch-up preservative application
  must be performed over water, then tarps or containers shall be used to capture any
  potential spills or drips.

  8.  Existing creosote-treated or ACZA-treated piles at the pier to be removed shall be
  removed and disposed of at a landfill authorized to accept such chemically treated
  waste.

Pier Pilings and Water Quality Requirements

Material used for construction of piers, pilings, docks, dolphins, or slips shall not include timber
preserved with creosote, (or similar petroleum-derived products). Pilings treated with Ammoniacal
Copper Arsenate (ACA), Ammoniacal Zinc Arsenate (ACZA) or Chromated Copper Arsenate
(CCA) shall be used only if wrapped or coated prior to installation with a water tight plastic sleeve,
or similar sealant. To prevent the introduction of toxins and debris into the marine environment,
the use of plastic wrapped pilings (e.g., PVC Pilewrap) and reinforced plastic for pilings (e.g., high
density polyethylene (HDPE) pile armor), shall conform to the following requirements:

  1. The material used shall be durable and a minimum of one-tenth of an inch thick.

SUBJECT:  Discuss Revisions to Article 3 of Chapter 1 of Title 3 of the Avalon
  Municipal Code Modifying the Transient Rental licensing system

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Review and discuss alternatives to proposed amendments to
transient rental licensing system. If consensus, recommend the Planning Commission consider
ordinance revisions regarding transient rental license regulations, and direct staff to revise the
ordinance.

REPORT SUMMARY: In 2020, the City of Avalon modified the process by which it monitors
and regulates transient rentals. Prior to 2020, transient rentals were authorized by Conditional
Use Permit, “CUP” under the City’s Zoning Code. On December 15, 2020, the City Council
adopted Ordinance No. 1192-20 (the “TRL Ordinance”), which modified the way that transient
rentals are approved in the City. These changes are now reflected in Article 3 of Chapter 3-1 of
Title 3 of the Avalon Municipal Code (AMC). In modifying the AMC, transient rentals would no
longer be authorized with a CUP, which runs with the land irrespective of intensity of use or
transfer of property ownership. Now, the City authorizes transient rentals through a Transient
Rental License (TRL) system that requires the applicant to annually seek re-approval of the
license.
Additionally, Article 3 of Chapter 3-1 of Title 3:
  • Allows existing compliant CUPs for transient rentals to remain valid until the second
  sale of the property to which the CUP is tied (the amortization period). Upon the
  second sale, the CUP expires, and the property owner must apply for a Transient
  Rental License.
  • Establishes guidelines and standards for the Planning Commission in deciding
  whether to approve the license (occupancy limits, management requirements,
  payment of transient occupancy tax, etc.). The City Council hears appeals from the
  Planning Commission’s decision.
  • Prohibits transfer of Transient Rental Licenses, except as otherwise provided.
  • Requires the Planning Commission to notice and hold a public hearing prior to
  approving a Transient Rental License.
  • Establishes a transient rental inspection program, sign requirements, advertising
  requirements, and other standards on the operation of an approved transient rental.
 Council amended the TRL Ordinance on November 16, 2021 to require that all transient rental
properties shall ensure a minimum of three nights per calendar year. The ordinance also
imposed penalties for not meeting that minimum requirement.

On August 1, 2023, the City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance #U-121223 establishing a 45-
day moratorium on the issuance of new Transient Rental Licenses.

On September 15, 2023, the City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance #U-1213-23, extending
the moratorium for an additional 10 month and 15-day period. This additional time was needed
to further determine the level of impact of Transient Rentals in the City of Avalon.

On August 6, 2024, the City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance #U-1220-24, extending the
moratorium until July 30, 2025 to allow City staff to develop a Transient License database and
complete a comprehensive inventory of Transient Rental Licenses and existing CUPs in
Avalon.

During the moratorium period, City Staff held two community/stakeholder meetings discussing
quality of life issues, financial benefits and impacts, and the sustainability and housing impacts
associated with transient rentals.

From December 1, 2023 to January 21, 2024, the City conducted a survey to determine the
overall impact of Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses amongst Island visitors,
residents and property owners. The survey also provided insight into participant’s thoughts
regarding potential enhanced regulations and/or additional enforcement. The City received 457
complete survey responses, but a total of 595 responses were submitted. Survey results were
presented to the Planning Commission on February 21, 2024 and provided to the City Council
on August 6, 2024.

When asked to rank the topics to be considered before imposing future short-term rental
regulation by order of importance, survey respondents ranked the top five topics as follows:

Considering the survey responses, stakeholder and community feedback, and a comprehensive
review of other California municipal short-term rental ordinances, City Staff recommends City
Council consider the following revisions to the Transient Rental License Ordinance:
  1. Modify the regulatory guidelines to implement a revocation policy based on non
  compliance with the City’s noise ordinance, responsiveness of property manager to
  complaints, and the City’s policies and procedures regarding trash, parking, etc.
  2. Establish an annual renewal license fee (i.e. $1 000) for all short-term rentals renting 20
  or more days a year. This fee will recoup expenses associated with City services (sewer,
  solid waste, LASD contract) as well as offset the cost of increased regulation and
  enforcement, administrative oversight, iWorq database, expanded Host Compliance
  agreement, and an inclusionary housing fee.
  3. Establish an annual renewal license fee (i.e. $250) for all short-term rentals renting fewer
  than 20 days a year to offset administrative costs, the cost to maintain the iWorq database
  and an inclusionary housing fee.
  a. Allow a waiver of the fee if the property owner provides proof that a long-term
  tenant is occupying the rental.
  4. Require all online short-term rental postings include property’s City of Avalon Business
  License Number. This will allow for more definitive tracking of short-term rentals.
  5. Require an on-site property manager meet the guest(s) and review the City’s rules and
  regulations and verify number of guests arriving are in compliance with unit’s occupancy
  limits.
  6. Establish a maximum number of short-term rentals in Avalon by an adopted resolution.
  (City-wide Cap). This resolution will be reviewed every two-years, or by the request of the
  City Council, to ensure the City is balancing the need to preserve affordable housing with the
  economic benefit of revenues derived from short term rentals.
   7. If City-wide Cap is adopted, implement a waitlist policy and annual procedure for
  monitoring the waitlist.

In order to establish a maximum cap of short-term rentals, in Spring 2024, the City contracted
with iWorks to assist in the development of a comprehensive database to assist in the
management and tracking of the City’s Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses.

Initially, an analysis was conducted by City Staff using the City’s business license database, as
well as transient rental license records, to identify a total number of short-term rentals in Avalon.
According to the analysis of the business license database and transient rental license records,
City Staff determined there are 373 properties with transient rental business licenses.
  • 260 are CUPs,
  • 29 are TRLs, and
  • 84 are “grandfathered.”

“Grandfathered” short-term rentals are rentals established before the 1994 modification of the
Avalon Municipal Code to permit short-term rentals by issuance of a CUP. City Staff
recommends that all “grandfathered” transient rental properties in good standing (with a valid
business license and actively paying TOT) be consolidated to be included on the City’s short-
term rental list and be treated as active CUP holders. As such, the grandfathered properties
would hold the ability to sell one time (amortization period).

To ensure that all CUPs have been identified and accounted for, City Staff took an additional
step of culling through more than 40 years of historical records detailing the issuance, transfer
and revocation of Conditional Use Permits within the City of Avalon.

After completing the analysis of historical records, City Staff identified an additional 62 properties
that have obtained a CUP; however, these properties are not active business license holders
and have not remitted TOT in recent history.

Before providing a recommendation to the City Council regarding a potential short-term rental
cap, City Staff would like to first commence the revocation process for any properties not in
compliance with the AMC, including those not holding an active business license and/or
nonpayment of TOT, staff action shall include seeking termination of CUPs that are not in
compliance with AMC § 9-8.4 1 1.

City Staff recommends that the City Council direct the Planning Commission consider the
proposed revisions to the AMC at their next regular meeting. Planning Commission’s
recommendations will be brought back to the City Council with a revised ordinance at a future
meeting.
